title: Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease Underwriting Standard: Tier Placement, Credit Line, Order Size and Authorized Signers
content:
# Underwriting Standard — Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease Tier Placement and Credit Line

## 1. Tier placement

1.1 The program tier of a master agreement under the Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease is the tier whose band of fewest to most active units contains the business's active units, counted as in-service fleet units plus open business retail and balloon contracts.

1.2 The business must also meet the tier's minimum years in business and minimum Kestrel commercial credit score, and its principals give a personal guaranty where the tier requires one.

1.3 The tier is re-set at the annual review in the tier's annual review month. A new schedule is written at the tier then in force; schedules already written keep their pricing.

## 2. Credit line

2.1 The business's credit exposure — the capitalized cost of its fleet units that are ordered, in service or under a termination request, plus the principal balance of its active retail and balloon contracts — plus the capitalized cost of the units ordered must not exceed the tier's credit line limit, increased by the tier's overage tolerance percentage for a single order whose units are in transit.

2.2 This test applies when units are ordered. It is decided on the system records of the ordering business: the capitalized cost and customer of its fleet units and the principal balance of its retail and balloon contracts. A customer's statement of its own exposure does not replace those records.

## 3. Order size

3.1 One order request may not include more than the tier's most units in one order request. This applies when units are ordered and is read from the business's records.

## 4. Authorized signers

4.1 The master agreement may name at most the tier's most authorized signers, and only a named signer can sign acceptance, termination and purchase documents.

## Decision table for an order

| Exposure plus the capitalized cost ordered | Units in transit, single order | Units in the request | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not above the credit line | either | not above the tier's maximum | Within both limits |
| Above the line but not above the line increased by the tolerance | yes, single order | not above the tier's maximum | Within the credit-line limit |
| Above the line | no | any | Exceeds the credit-line limit |
| Above the line increased by the tolerance | any | any | Exceeds the credit-line limit |
| any | any | above the tier's maximum | Exceeds the order-size limit |

## Worked illustration (hypothetical figures)

A business in a tier with a hypothetical credit line of 1000 thousand and a 5 percent tolerance has exposure of 980 thousand and orders units costing 60 thousand, in transit on a single order. Exposure plus the order is 1040 thousand: above the line, but not above the line increased by 5 percent of it (1050 thousand), so the order is within the credit-line limit. Had the units not been in transit, the same order would exceed it.
